provenance.statement: Let users export their invoices as CSV. It must reuse the existing Report Builder and finish in under 10 seconds for 10,000 rows.

assumptions: "Users" means authenticated users of the application exporting their own invoices.
"Invoices" refers to an existing invoice data set already available to the system.

ambiguities.question: Which users may export invoices (all users, specific roles, or only the owner of each invoice)?
Which invoice fields and columns must the CSV contain, and in what order?
Should the export cover all of a user's invoices, or can the user filter by date range, status, or customer?
How does the user trigger the export (UI button, API endpoint, or both), and how is the file delivered (direct download, email, or link)?
What hardware, load, and measurement conditions apply to the 10-second requirement for 10,000 rows (for example, end-to-end or server-side only, and at what percentile)?
What is the required behavior for exports above 10,000 rows?
What CSV format details are required (encoding, delimiter, header row, date and currency formatting, escaping)?

acceptance_criteria.statement: Users can export their invoices as a CSV file.
The invoice CSV export is implemented by reusing the existing Report Builder rather than a separate export mechanism.
Exporting 10,000 invoice rows to CSV completes in under 10 seconds.
